Builders — Carpenters, Laborers and Masons

UBC carpenters, LIUNA laborers, BAC bricklayers and IUOE operators

OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subparts Q (concrete and formwork), L (scaffolds), CC (cranes) and 1926.1153 respirable crystalline silica; ANSI A10.9 concrete and masonry; the engineer's shoring and reshoring drawings

The building trades' own stations: formwork and shoring to the engineer's drawings, a mass-timber panel picked and set, and masonry on a scaffold under the silica rule — beside the concrete pour and scaffold erection the construction programme already teaches.

What it proves

Competency: Form, shore, set and cut to the engineer's drawings without breathing silica

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 2 of its 4 stations, against OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart Q Concrete and masonry construction; OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart L Scaffolds; OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1153 Respirable crystalline silica; ANSI/ASSP A10.9 Safety Requirements for Concrete and Masonry Work.

These stations also count toward:

  • Fall Protection (2 of this track's stations count toward it)
  • Crane and Rigging — the lift plan, the load and the landing (1 of this track's stations count toward it)
  • Respiratory Protection — selection, proving and working on air (1 of this track's stations count toward it)

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subparts Q (concrete and formwork), L (scaffolds), CC (cranes) and 1926.1153 respirable crystalline silica; ANSI A10.9 concrete and masonry; the engineer's shoring and reshoring drawings. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
